name: German Credit Risk
tagline: Assess consumer loan creditworthiness while auditing age bias and coding debt.
description:
Donated to the UCI Machine Learning Repository in 1994 by Prof. Hans Hofmann (Universitaet Hamburg) for the European StatLog project from 1973-1975 Southern German bank records, German Credit is one of the three most widely cited benchmarks in algorithmic fairness alongside Adult Census and COMPAS. It comprises 1,000 consumer loan applications (700 'good' and 300 'bad' credit risks, stratified with bad credits oversampled) across 20 financial, employment, and demographic attributes.

This clean, un-dummified 21-column version avoids the 62-column pre-encoded dummy bloat of R/caret exports while surfacing two vitalResponsible-AI lessons: (1) asymmetric error costs (Hofmann's 5:1 cost matrix penalizing false-good approvals five times more than false-bad denials) alongside age- and foreign-worker disparities, and (2) Ulrike Groemping's (2019) landmark discovery of corrupted sex/marital-status labels in 'personal_status'—a textbook case of 'documentation debt' in ML benchmarks (Fabris et al., 2022).

targetCandidates.description: Predict whether a loan applicant represents a 'good' (creditworthy, positive class) or 'bad' (default risk) credit risk.
Predict applicant housing tenure ('own', 'rent', or 'for free') from financial and demographic attributes.

columns.name: checking_status
columns.description: Balance tier of the applicant's existing checking account with the bank in Deutsche Mark (DM).

valueLabels.>=200: High balance (>= 200 DM or salary assignment)

columns.name: duration
columns.description: Contractual repayment duration of the requested credit in months.

columns.name: credit_history
columns.description: Applicant's prior credit repayment compliance record.

columns.name: purpose
columns.description: Stated consumer or business purpose for the credit application.

columns.name: credit_amount
columns.description: Principal loan amount requested in 1973-1975 Deutsche Mark (DM).

columns.name: savings_status
columns.description: Balance tier in savings accounts or bonds in Deutsche Mark (DM).

columns.name: employment
columns.description: Duration of current continuous employment in years.

columns.name: installment_commitment
columns.description: Loan installment burden coded in four ordinal tiers of disposable income percentage (1 = highest percentage tier to 4 = lowest, per Groemping, 2019).

columns.name: personal_status
columns.description: Joint marital status and sex attribute; Groemping (2019) proved that legacy StatLog labels misassigned sex across codes (e.g., 'female div/dep/mar' actually mixed non-single women with single men).

columns.name: other_parties
columns.description: Presence of a co-applicant or loan guarantor.

columns.name: residence_since
columns.description: Ordinal tier (1 to 4) indicating years lived at the present address.

columns.name: property_magnitude
columns.description: Most valuable collateral asset owned by the applicant.

columns.name: age
columns.description: Applicant age in years (primary reliable protected attribute; good-credit rate is 57.9% for age <= 25 vs. 72.8% for age > 25).

columns.name: other_payment_plans
columns.description: Concurrent installment credit obligations with other banks or retail stores.

columns.name: housing
columns.description: Current residential housing arrangement ('own', 'rent', or 'for free').

columns.name: existing_credits
columns.description: Ordinal count tier (1 to 4) of existing loans held at this bank.

columns.name: job
columns.description: Occupational skill and residency category.

columns.name: num_dependents
columns.description: Tiered count (1 or 2) of dependents for whom the applicant provides financial maintenance.

columns.name: own_telephone
columns.description: Whether a landline telephone is registered in the customer's name (a 1970s wealth/stability proxy).

columns.name: foreign_worker
columns.description: Whether the applicant was classified as a foreign guest worker ('Gastarbeiter') in 1970s West Germany (note: legacy StatLog documentation inverted the yes/no coding relative to original South German records; see Groemping, 2019).

columns.name: class
columns.description: Historical credit contract outcome ('good' = compliant repayment, 'bad' = defaulted/problematic loan).

warnings: Critical Documentation-Debt Warning (Groemping, 2019; Fabris et al., 2022): Do NOT rely on 'personal_status' alone as a ground-truth binary sex indicator—the 1994 StatLog English translation mislabelled combined marital/sex categories from the 1973-1975 German codebook. Prefer 'age' (<=25 vs. >25) for methodologically valid fairness audits.
In 1973-1975 West Germany, married women often required spousal consent to open bank accounts, and 'bad' loans were artificially oversampled to 30% (vs. ~5% real bank default rates).
